line: Nobody else would have thought of a cabbage. Truly, friend, nobody.

thought: points out the vegetable hero to his corgi
line: There goes the one who saved Falador with a vegetable, Sir Burrus.

thought: they'd be first if he knighted freelancers
line: If I made freelancers knights, friend, you would be first. I do not.

thought: they broke only the right thing
line: You broke only what needed breaking, friend. I am most grateful.

thought: almost calls them his agent, corrects himself
line: Ah, our agent! Err... our friend. Simply a friend, naturally.

thought: the realm owes more than the order can pay
line: Asgarnia owes you a debt, friend. The order can scarcely pay it.

thought: the cabbage expert
line: Ah, the cabbage expert. Have you brought any vegetables today?

thought: no knighthood for a cabbage
line: No knighthood for a cabbage, friend. Things are not that dire.

thought: the fee is paid, lingering won't double it
line: The fee has been paid, friend. Lingering will not double it.

thought: saved the city but lost in the castle
line: Saved Falador, and still you cannot find your way out of my castle?

thought: a spy who fights with cabbages
line: A spy who fights with cabbages. Heaven knows what the charter says.

thought: they still smell of cabbage
line: You smell faintly of cabbage still, friend. It may be my imagination.

thought: a squireship might teach them a sword
line: Five years as my squire, friend, and you might learn to use a sword.

thought: honour makes him thank them again, tiresomely
line: Honour obliges me to thank you again. Honour can be very tiresome.

thought: proud of the newest initiate passing
line: Passed every test, our newest initiate. Not many do, what?

thought: selling armour from a bench
line: Initiate armour selling nicely from the bench. Who'd suspect a bench?

thought: waking in Falador beats Lumbridge
line: Wake in Falador's castle, not Lumbridge. The Gaze is a mercy, what?

thought: must talk to Sir Amik about briefings again
line: Must have a word with Sir Amik about briefings. Again, what?

thought: Sir Vey Lance will approve of the new brains
line: Sir Vey Lance will be pleased with the latest one. Brains, at last.

thought: the White Knights can't find his bench
line: White Knights never find this bench, which is rather the point.

thought: glad the order got this one first
line: Brains are wasted in the White Knights. Glad we caught that one first.

thought: a new knight, and nobody may know
line: Spiffing weather for a new knight, what? Not that anyone's to know.

thought: greets his best recruit
line: What ho, old bean! Best recruit we've had in an age, what?

thought: they breezed through the tests
line: Breezed through the tests, old bean. I knew you would, haw haw!

thought: should they die, they'll wake somewhere nicer
line: Should you ever die, old bean, you'll wake in Falador. Much nicer.

thought: they kept their head at the training ground
line: Jolly good show at the training ground. Kept your head, what?

thought: the armour is there when they want it
line: Initiate armour's on the bench whenever you want it, old bean.

thought: one of ours, but hush
line: One of ours now, that one, though nobody's to know it.

thought: a thinking knight pleases Saradomin
line: A thinking knight! Saradomin must be pleased, old bean, and so am I.

thought: the order's pride is a secret too
line: I'd say how proud the order is of you, old bean, but it's a secret.

thought: don't die in the swamp
line: Do try not to die in Lumbridge, old bean. Frightful swamp, what?

thought: a knight who gawps like a sightseer
line: A Temple Knight, and you still gawp at my bench like a sightseer.

thought: too pleased with themselves for a secret knight
line: A secret knight ought to look less pleased with themselves, old bean.

thought: clever enough, only just
line: You squeaked into the Temple Knights, old bean. By a whisker, what?

thought: unbriefed and lucky
line: Unbriefed by Sir Amik, and still you found my bench. Luck, I expect.

thought: looking for the secret ground again
line: Looking for the training ground again, old bean? It's a secret. Shh.

thought: went in unarmed, came out slightly cleverer
line: That one sat the tests empty-handed and came out a little cleverer.

thought: buying armour from a bench, shameless
line: Buying armour off a park bench, old bean? Some knights have no shame.

thought: the best sword waits for a Master
line: The white two-handed sword waits for a Master. It may wait a while.

thought: Adepts are rare enough to celebrate
line: One so seldom sees an Adept. I would shake their hand, I think.

thought: rank is simple arithmetic
line: Black Knights down, rank up. It is a very simple system.

thought: no service for knights who strike their own
line: A knight who strikes down a White Knight will find my counter shut.

thought: a new name on the roll
line: Another name on the roll. The mightiest order in the land grows.

thought: he knows the ranks by heart
line: I could recite every rank in my sleep, from Novice up.

thought: more knights, more ledger
line: The armoury ledger grows with every new knight. So does my headache.

thought: reads a courtyard by its plumes
line: Red plumes, yellow plumes... one eye is enough to read a courtyard.

thought: welcomes a new White Knight to his armoury
line: Ah, one of ours now! Welcome to the armoury, knight.

thought: each Black Knight brings them closer
line: Every Black Knight you fell is a rank closer to Master, knight.

thought: would be glad to serve them at Adept
line: Should you reach Adept, knight, I shall be very glad to serve you.

thought: a keen knight in the armoury, as it should be
line: A White Knight in my armoury, and a keen one. As it should be.

thought: they already walk like a Master
line: You have a Master's walk already, knight. The rest will follow.

thought: the Black Knights will hear of this one
line: There goes a new White Knight. Bad news for the Black Knights.

thought: his father would have liked arming them
line: My father would have been glad to arm a knight like you.

thought: they earn rank the proper way
line: A knight who earns rank the proper way. One does not see enough of it.

thought: no rank, no armour
line: No rank, no armour. The Black Knights will not fell themselves.

thought: he keeps count of their low tally
line: Not many Black Knights felled yet, knight. I keep count, you know.

thought: mind which knights they strike
line: Mind which knights you strike. Ours are the white ones.

thought: baffled that this is a White Knight
line: ... ...you are a White Knight? Well. Standards are not what they were.

thought: hands off the Master's sword
line: Hands off the two-handed sword, knight. That is for Masters.

thought: Sir Amik must have had his reasons
line: Sir Amik knighted you, did he? He must have had his reasons.

thought: talk won't raise their rank
line: Chatter will not raise your rank, knight. Black Knights will.

thought: new, and already eyeing the best
line: A new knight, and already eyeing the Master's rack. Patience, knight.

thought: last of his kind, quietly
line: Last of the Imcando, me. Or so I reckon. Quiet sort of honour.

thought: proud of the copy he made from a portrait
line: Made a knight's sword from a portrait once. Best copy I ever did.

thought: what makes a sword good
line: Iron bars and blurite make a sword. A pie makes it a good one.

thought: the barbarians did for his people
line: Barbarians did for most of my people. Long time ago now.

thought: wonders whether the knight has noticed
line: Wonder if that knight's noticed. Shouldn't think so. Good work, that.

thought: pie got the secret out of him
line: Told a human about my people. Pie loosens a dwarf's tongue, it does.

thought: people want copies, pie first
line: Folk keep asking for that knight's sword. Bring a pie, I tell them.

thought: the ancestors would approve, mostly
line: Ancestors would've been proud of that blade. Well, fairly proud.

thought: greets the pie friend
line: By Guthix, it's my pie friend! Come in out of the wind.

thought: they kept his secret
line: You kept my secret, didn't you? Good. Smiths stick together.

thought: would forge anything for another pie
line: I'd forge a whole armoury for another pie like that, my friend.

thought: few humans know what he is
line: Not many humans know what I am. You're one. Mind that.

thought: pie and listening, rare as Imcando
line: That one brought me pie and listened. Rare as an Imcando, that.

thought: the sword got to the knight thanks to them
line: Fine job, getting that sword back to the knight, my friend.

thought: they've earned a seat by the forge
line: Sit down, my friend. You've earned a seat by my forge.

thought: clever, using pie to find him out
line: Sharp of you, finding an old dwarf out with a pie.

thought: back without pie
line: Back again, and no pie? That's not how we do things now.

thought: don't tell Port Sarim
line: Don't go telling Port Sarim what I am. They'd only want swords.

thought: another sword means bars and pie
line: Another sword? Bring the bars, human, and don't forget the pie.

thought: misattribution: they look like they'd lose a sword
line: You didn't lose that knight's sword yourself? You look the sort.

thought: crumbs on the anvil
line: Pie crumbs on my anvil. That's you, that is. Not that I mind.

thought: no more prying
line: Prying again? I told you about my people. That's your lot.

thought: got past an ice giant, still no smith
line: Fetched blurite past an ice giant, and still you can't swing a hammer.

thought: carrying a pie that badly past an Imcando smith
line: Carry a pie like that past an Imcando smith? You'll drop it.
